# Style and Content Adaptation

Also called: Style Adaptation via Diffusion Guidance, Reference Image Conditioning

## Overview
Style and Content Adaptation modifies a pre-trained radiance field to incorporate specific visual styles or object contents by leveraging external conditions, such as reference images or text prompts, during the optimization loop. It distinguishes itself from sibling methods like [SKED](12268-sked.md) and [Single-Image Textual Inversion](19221-single-image-textual-inversion.md) by explicitly using reference images as conditional priors to guide the diffusion model's denoising process, ensuring the generated content adheres to the visual characteristics of the reference rather than relying solely on textual descriptions or single-view embeddings.

## Shared principles
The family shares a common optimization framework where a frozen diffusion model (typically Stable Diffusion) provides gradient signals to update the radiance field parameters. The core mechanism involves rendering an image from the current radiance field state, passing it through the diffusion model to compute a Score Distillation Sampling (SDS) loss or similar gradient, and backpropagating this signal to the radiance field. The key differentiator for this family is the conditioning mechanism: instead of using only a text prompt, the diffusion model is conditioned on a reference image $I_{ref}$ alongside the text prompt $T$. This is typically achieved by concatenating the reference image features or using it as an additional input to the UNet's cross-attention or spatial attention layers, thereby constraining the generated noise prediction to match the style or content of $I_{ref}$.

## Subtopics

### SKED
SKED [12268-sked.md] focuses on localized 3D editing using multi-view 2D sketches as spatial priors. It minimizes a composite loss $L = L_{SDS} + \lambda_s L_{sil} + \lambda_p L_{pres}$, where $L_{SDS}$ steers the content via diffusion, $L_{sil}$ ensures the rendered silhouette matches the sketch mask $M_v$, and $L_{pres}$ maintains fidelity to the original scene outside the sketch regions. It is chosen when precise spatial control over object insertion or replacement is required.

### [Single-Image Textual Inversion](19221-single-image-textual-inversion.md)
Single-Image Textual Inversion [19221-single-image-textual-inversion.md] optimizes a learnable token embedding $\langle e \rangle$ from a single input image to serve as a custom prompt. It solves the ill-posed nature of single-view reconstruction by providing an image-specific prompt that reduces artifacts like "floaters" and the "Janus problem." It is chosen when the goal is to generate novel views of a specific object from a single image without explicit 3D supervision.

### Style Adaptation via Diffusion Guidance
This variant uses a reference image as a condition alongside the text prompt to guide generation [S1]. By utilizing reference images as conditions, the method ensures that the generated content (e.g., "a stone chair") closely resembles the visual characteristics (material, texture) of the reference image (e.g., a stone), compared to results generated without a reference. This is implemented by incorporating the reference image into the diffusion model's conditioning pipeline, often via cross-attention or feature concatenation, to transfer style attributes to the radiance field optimization.

## Background
The concept of using external priors for radiance field editing and generation has evolved from text-only guidance to multi-modal conditioning. The specific use of reference images for style adaptation in the context of NeRFs is detailed in GO-NeRF [S1], which demonstrated that reference images can effectively guide the generation of objects with specific visual properties (e.g., material appearance) within a virtual reality content creation pipeline. This approach addresses the limitations of text-only prompts, which may lack the precision required for specific material or stylistic replication.
